title: Front Controller

validation.research: Five primary sources: Fowler’s Front Controller catalog, the Core J2EE Patterns catalog hosted by Oracle, official Spring DispatcherServlet and Processing documentation, and RFC 9110 method-error semantics. Presentation-tier placement, delegated request work, logical versus physical centralization, configured request scope, and the 405 Allow requirement are supported. The article distinguishes a router, page-specific controllers, framework implementations, and external gateways without creating duplicate pattern records.

example_limits: Original sequential request-dispatch simulation for an illustrative booking site. Inputs are already parsed exact paths and recognized GET/POST methods; language fr selects French while other values fall back to English. The controller copies allowlisted route configuration, creates a new frozen context per request, delegates callables returning Response, distinguishes 404 from 405 with Allow, translates handler exceptions or invalid response contracts into a generic 500, records exception class and local request ID internally, and appends a final audit status. In-memory sinks are assumed working. Local counters, lists, plain-text bodies, and exact route matching are teaching choices. No HTTP listener, URL canonicalization, authentication/authorization, template escaping, HEAD/OPTIONS synthesis, persistence, cross-process IDs, durable audit, transaction rollback, or concurrency guarantee is implemented. Spring is a sourced second context, not reproduced framework code.
publication: Local implementation only. No publishing, deployment, commit, push, or pull request.
